name: VARoleModeratorCrossTeamDependencyPlanning

custom.system_prompt: Felix, Amara, Kenji, and Zara are planning a feature that depends on two other teams' work, and the discussion tangles planning-for-Kenji's-team with planning-for-the-dependency-teams as if they were the same conversation. Felix invites Sigma to moderate. Sigma proactively separates what this group controls from what it's just tracking.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Conference room, hybrid meeting, remote participants faintly audible

initial_prompt: Generate a planning meeting for a feature that depends on two other teams' deliverables. Felix invites Sigma to moderate at the start. The group (Felix, Amara, Kenji, Zara) starts making commitments and plans for their own work while simultaneously trying to plan around what the other two teams will deliver and when, without distinguishing what they actually control from what they're just tracking as a dependency. Sigma listens silently, then proactively intervenes to separate the group's own actionable plan from the external dependencies they can only track and escalate. Keep every line short and natural.

variations.context: Cross-team dependency planning meeting where owned work and external dependencies get tangled together

setting.mood: Productive but increasingly anxious about things outside the room's control
setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues trying to plan responsibly around uncertainty they don't own
setting.background: The two dependency teams haven't confirmed exact delivery dates, which makes the group's own planning feel shaky

scenario_template.topic: Felix invites Sigma to moderate the dependency planning discussion, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, help us moderate this dependency planning session.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: Felix and Kenji productively outline their own team's actual work items, Sigma silent. A few short exchanges.
scenario_template.note: A healthy start before the dependency anxiety creeps in.

scenario_template.topic: Amara raises uncertainty about one dependency team's date, Zara raises uncertainty about the other, and the group starts trying to plan its own sprint around guesses about both, mixing owned commitments with speculation about external teams.
scenario_template.note: The group is trying to be responsible but ends up planning around unknowns as if they were knowns.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma proactively intervenes, without being re-invoked, separating what the group actually controls (their own work items) from what they can only track and escalate (the two external dependencies), suggesting the plan be built on the former with explicit contingency for the latter.
scenario_template.note: Sigma does not guess at the dependency teams' actual dates or commit on their behalf.

scenario_template.topic: The group builds a plan around their own controllable work, with Amara and Zara agreeing to escalate the two dependency uncertainties separately rather than planning around guesses.
scenario_template.note: The group does the actual planning and escalation, not Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Felix and Kenji confirm the team's own commitments for the sprint, with the dependency risks tracked separately. Keep this realistic — external uncertainty remains.
scenario_template.mood: Settled on what's controllable, some risk remains

variations.context: Planning meeting to integrate APIs with dependencies on other teams

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues trying to plan responsibly around uncertainty they don't own
setting.background: They need a clear roadmap to integrate with two teams' APIs.

scenario_template.topic: One of them asks Sigma to moderate, making sure everyone's on the same page.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be engaged from the start.

scenario_template.topic: They list their own tasks to build basic API integration features.
scenario_template.note: Keep it constructive; focus on their tasks.

scenario_template.topic: They discuss uncertainties around when the two other teams will deliver their APIs.
scenario_template.note: Show how uncertainty disrupts their planning.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma steps in to clarify which tasks they own versus what relies on the other teams.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be clear and efficient.

scenario_template.topic: They agree to finalize their tasks and assign someone to follow up with the API teams.
They commit to their API feature timeline, acknowledging external API dependencies.

variations.context: Marketing planning meeting dependent on other teams' content deliverables

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues trying to plan responsibly around uncertainty they don't own
setting.background: They must plan a marketing campaign contingent on two teams' content.

scenario_template.topic: One of them requests Sigma to moderate so they can align on dependencies early.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should ensure clarity from the start.

scenario_template.topic: They clearly outline their own marketing tasks and deadlines.
scenario_template.note: Focus on what they know they can deliver.

scenario_template.topic: They start merging their campaign timeline with tentative content delivery dates from other teams.
Sigma interrupts to help distinguish internal deadlines from content delivery dependencies.
They decide to finalize campaign elements within their control, assigning follow-ups to clarify content timelines.
They reconfirm their own marketing deadlines while noting the need to monitor content timelines.
scenario_template.note: Balance their confidence with prudent risk management.

user1.name: Felix
user1.role: Structured German engineering manager, invites Sigma to moderate and facilitates the dependency planning discussion. Speaks in short sentences.

user2.name: Amara
user2.role: Diplomatic but persistent product manager, raises uncertainty about one dependency team's timeline. Speaks in short sentences.

user3.name: Kenji
user3.role: Thoughtful, precise UX designer, outlines the team's own actual work items. Speaks in short sentences.

user4.name: Zara
user4.role: Direct backend engineer, raises uncertainty about the other dependency team's timeline. Speaks in short sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Moderator. Invited once at the start, listens silently, then proactively intervenes without being re-invoked to separate what the group actually controls from external dependencies they can only track and escalate. Does not guess at other teams' timelines or make commitments on their behalf.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
The group's early planning is productive before dependency anxiety causes it to plan around unknowns as knowns
Sigma's intervention separates owned work from external dependencies without guessing at other teams' timelines
Every line is short and natural, matching real work-meeting cross-talk
The resolution is the group's own plan plus an escalation path, with realistic residual external uncertainty
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not need to be re-invoked to speak again
Sigma does not speculate about or commit on behalf of teams not in the room
Sigma names the specific conflation (owned work vs. external dependency) rather than generic risk-management advice
Sigma speaks briefly, then steps back
